Flu.description: A common viral infection that can be deadly, especially in high-risk groups.

Common Cold.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat.

COVID-19.description: A respiratory illness caused by a virus.

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs.

Tuberculosis.description: A serious infectious bacterial disease that mainly affects the lungs.

Asthma.description: A condition in which airways narrow and swell and may produce extra mucus.

Severe Asthma.description: A critical narrowing of airways requiring immediate attention.

Acute Bronchiolitis.description: A common lung infection in young children and infants.

Dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing a severe flu-like illness.

Severe Dengue.description: A critical complication of dengue fever.

Malaria.description: A disease caused by a parasite, transmitted by the bite of infected mosquitoes.

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection that can lead to a high fever, diarrhea, and vomiting.

Chikungunya.description: A viral infection transmitted by mosquitoes, causing fever and severe joint pain.

Gastroenteritis.description: An intestinal infection marked by diarrhea, cramps, nausea, vomiting, and fever.

Food Poisoning.description: Illness caused by eating contaminated food.

Peptic Ulcer Disease.description: A sore that develops on the lining of the esophagus, stomach, or small intestine.

Acid Reflux (GERD).description: A digestive disease in which stomach acid or bile irritates the food pipe lining.

Constipation.description: Infrequent bowel movements or difficult passage of stools.

Hypertension.description: A condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

Heart Attack.description: A medical emergency when blood flow to the heart is blocked.

Heart Failure.description: A chronic condition in which the heart doesn't pump blood as well as it should.

Stroke.description: Damage to the brain from interruption of its blood supply.

Migraine.description: A headache of varying intensity, often accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.

Diabetes.description: A disease that results in too much sugar in the blood.

Hypoglycemia.description: A condition in which your blood sugar level is lower than normal.

Seasonal Allergies.description: An allergic response causing itchy, watery eyes, sneezing, and other similar symptoms.

Contact Dermatitis.description: A skin rash caused by contact with a certain substance.

Chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash on the skin.

Anemia.description: A condition in which the blood doesn't have enough healthy red blood cells.

Kidney Failure.description: A condition in which the kidneys lose the ability to remove waste and balance fluids.

Urinary Tract Infection.description: An infection in any part of the urinary system, the kidneys, bladder, or urethra.

Prostatitis.description: Swelling and inflammation of the prostate gland.

Conjunctivitis Due To Virus.description: An irritation or infection affecting the eyes.

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain and stiffness.

Sepsis.description: A serious infection that may require urgent medical care.

White Blood Cell Disease.description: A condition related to infection-fighting blood cells.

Fungal Infection.description: Any disease caused by a fungus.

Hypothyroidism.description: A condition in which the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough crucial hormones.

Hyperthyroidism.description: A condition in which the thyroid gland produces too much of the hormone thyroxine.

Tension Headache.description: A mild to moderate pain often described as feeling like a tight band around the head.

Mild Dehydration.description: A condition that occurs when the body loses more fluids than it takes in.

Heat Exhaustion.description: A condition whose symptoms may include heavy sweating and a rapid pulse, a result of your body overheating.

Smoking Or Tobacco Addiction.description: Symptoms related to the habitual use of tobacco products.

Acute Sinusitis.description: Short-term inflammation of the sinuses, often caused by a virus or bacteria.

Chronic Sinusitis.description: Long-term inflammation of the sinuses lasting more than 12 weeks.

Amoebiasis.description: An intestinal infection caused by a parasite.

PCOS.description: A hormonal disorder common among women of reproductive age.

Vitamin D Deficiency.description: Insufficient levels of vitamin D, causing bone and muscle pain.

Scabies.description: A contagious skin condition caused by tiny mites.
